reason: The warm afternoon sets up the heat response described in the goal.
expectation: The body will experience warmth, preparing it to respond by sweating.

effect: The warming is sensed by the skin and hypothalamus, setting up a response.
reaction: The link from skin signals to the hypothalamus is clear.
reason: Sweat glands are the direct next step toward the evaporation goal.
expectation: The warming signal will activate sweating at the skin.

effect: The attempt instead widened skin vessels, bringing more blood and heat toward the surface; sweating may now be available.
reaction: I was surprised the vessel response came before sweating.
reason: Sweat glands are still the visible next component for the evaporation goal.
expectation: The glands will produce sweat on the warmed skin.

effect: Sweat has reached the skin surface; evaporation is still needed to carry heat away.
reaction: The distinction between sweating and evaporation is clear.
reason: Air at the skin shows water molecules lifting away from a wet patch, matching the goal.
expectation: Sweat will evaporate and carry heat away from the body.

effect: Evaporation carried heat away, and the new goal shifts attention to the cold response.
reaction: The fading sweat signal makes the feedback response clear.
reason: The cold evening sets up the temperature change needed for the new goal.
expectation: The body will sense the colder surroundings and begin a cold response.

effect: Cold sensing reduced the signal to sweat glands; the body still needs responses that conserve and generate heat.
reaction: The reduced sweating is a clear first response to cooling.
reason: Skin vessels changed blood flow during warming, so they are a plausible next step for conserving heat in the cold.
expectation: Skin vessels will narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

effect: Skin vessel narrowing reduces heat loss but does not produce heat, so heat generation remains.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and making heat is useful.
reason: Skeletal muscle is the remaining visible component and can generate heat through shivering.
expectation: Muscle contractions will generate heat in response to the cold.

effect: Shivering completed the cold response: repeated muscle contractions use ATP and produce heat alongside reduced heat loss.
reaction: The contrast between conserving heat and generating it was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following both cold responses was worthwhile: the planned illustrations distinguish narrowed vessels reducing heat loss from muscle contractions producing heat.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial attempt to activate sweat glands was less worthwhile because the game required the vessel response first, although its compatibility feedback immediately performed that step.

surprise.text: I expected sweating to follow warming directly, so I was surprised that skin circulation had to change first.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the vessel response before sweating felt somewhat arbitrary: the feedback showed what was allowed, but did not explain why that order was necessary.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the warm-to-cold comparison and feedback illustrations made the constructions useful, though the forced ordering left limited room for decisions.
